name: Nova-C

solarArrayW.note: Derived from the FCC IM-1 application (Intuitive Machines): "Three fixed body-mounted solar panels provide a maximum of 788 W", read as the summed rating of the three panels at normal incidence. In our model solarArrayW is the output at the best polar Sun direction (el 0–10°) for this layout: 788 W × K = 788 × 0.626 = 494 W (K from the assumed panel layout, see panels). Team decision 2026-11-15. Lower bound for comparison (SOLAR what-if): Intuitive Machines' 2019 release, "At least 200 watts of power on the surface" (collectSPACE repost; astronomy.com 2025: "afford 200 watts").

panels.note: Team description: 3 fixed panels (FCC IM-1 application confirms three fixed body-mounted solar panels; their directions are not published), 1 on the top deck and 2 on side walls of the hexagonal body, no Sun tracking (tip-overs of IM-1 and IM-2 cut their power). astronomy.com (2025): "one on the lander's top deck, plus two body-mounted arrays". Assumed: the two walls are adjacent (60° apart) and the 3 panels share the output equally.

batteryWh.note: FCC IM-1 application: three fixed body-mounted solar panels, Li-ion batteries with a total energy capacity of 1554 Wh, 28 VDC bus (ODAR: three 518 Wh battery assemblies). Replaces the earlier 700 Wh derived from 25 Ah × 28 V (secondary sources).

batteryRoundTripEff.note: Li-ion class value, not published for this lander: energy out / energy in of the cells. LLNL LEO tests (Mayer, Feikert, Kaschmitter): 86% called very good, 91% at 30% depth of discharge. Split evenly between charge and discharge (sqrt 0.9 each); power-electronics losses not included.

survivalLoadW.note: 1554 Wh / ~15 h (IM: comms 10–20 h after sunset)

designedForNight.note: battery limits — cannot survive lunar night

panelHeightM.note: Height of the solar panels (and antenna) above the ground used for the terrain horizon. Not published; assumed: the wall panels, which collect almost all power with the Sun a few degrees above the horizon, are centred at about half the vehicle height (3.94 m, FCC IM-1 application) → 2 m. Robustness row: 1 m and 3 m.

landingAccuracyM.note: Radius of the landing ellipse the verdict is re-checked over. IM-2 Athena (6 Mar 2025, Mons Mouton) landed more than 400 m from its target according to NASA (Intuitive Machines: 250 m); IM-1 (Feb 2024) came down ~1.5 km off after a laser rangefinder failure.

heatLossW.note: Heat the warm box radiates at +20 °C to a cold sky. Assumed: the radiators are sized to reject the day load (150 W) and keep radiating at night (no louvers or heat switches; CLPS landers are designed for daylight). At the -20 °C set point that is 83 W, minus what the ground gives back (LRO Diviner).

heatCapacityKJPerK.note: Thermal mass of the warm box: 10% of the dry mass assumed coupled to it (batteries, avionics, nearby structure), at aluminium's 0.897 kJ/(kg·K) → 60.5 kJ/K. Dry mass: sourced dry mass 675 kg (Wikipedia, Structure: "a dry mass of 675 kg"). Sets how long the box coasts after sunset before the heaters switch on.

operatingTempC.note: Warm-box temperature while lit and when darkness begins: within the 10–25 °C range recommended for long Li-ion battery life (EnerSys ABSL space battery datasheet). Not published for this lander.

minTempC.note: Heater set point: the box (battery) is never let below it at night. Space Li-ion cells are characterised for discharge at -20 °C and below (EnerSys, Space Power Workshop 2022); charging needs 0 °C or more, which the Sun brings back. Not published for this lander.

groundViewFactor.note: Share of the warm box's radiating area that sees the ground (side walls half ground, half sky; top deck sky; bottom ground). The rest radiates to the ~3 K sky. Geometric estimate.

modelCredit: Model: concept image Meshy AI · 3D Microsoft TRELLIS.2 (MIT) · stylized, not manufacturer CAD
modelNote: Visualisation only. Bounding-box height scaled to 3.94 m: FCC IM-1 application gives Nova-C as 2.19 m × 2.385 m × 3.938 m (https://apps.fcc.gov/els/GetAtt.html?amp=&id=266519&x=). modelNozzleOffsetM: engine plume origin above the feet, visual estimate from the model's shape.

name: Blue Ghost

panels.note: Team description: 3 fixed panels on the top deck and the side walls, at different angles, powering the lander from sunrise to sunset without rotating mechanisms (Blue Ghost M1). Assumed: the side panels face opposite directions and the 3 panels share the output equally.

batteryWh.note: survivalLoadW × ~5 h night ops observed on M1

batteryRoundTripEff.note: Li-ion class value, not published for this lander: energy out / energy in of the cells. missionDurationDays.note: M1: 14+ days daylight + ~5 h into night

designedForNight.note: M1 configuration ended ~5 h after sunset

Robustness row: 0 m and 2 m.

name: Griffin

solarArrayW.note: Class estimate: output not published. Astrobotic Lunar Landers PUG (2021) p. 28: Griffin "is designed to be power positive" on the surface (so the array must exceed the ~700 W day load) and "can be configured to carry larger solar arrays" than Peregrine.

panels.note: Team description: one large fixed panel on one side, optimised for polar missions; the lander yaws before touchdown so the panel faces the Sun. Astrobotic Lunar Landers PUG (2021) pp. 24, 28: polar missions "utilize side-mounted panels" (the Griffin Mission One configuration). Assumed: one vertical panel carries the whole output (count, size and tilt not published).

batteryRoundTripEff.note: Li-ion class value, not published for this lander: energy out / energy in of the cells. LLNL LEO tests (Mayer, Feikert, Kaschmitter): 86% called very good, 91% at 30% depth of discharge. Split evenly between charge and discharge (sqrt 0.9 each); power-electronics losses not included.

dayLoadW.note: Payload power from the Astrobotic Lunar Landers PUG (2021) p. 55: NOMINAL 1.0 W per kg of payload (PEAK 2.5 W/kg as scheduled) × 625 kg polar capacity (p. 24) = 625 W, plus ~75 W for the lander bus (assumption, not published).

missionDurationDays.note: Astrobotic Lunar Landers PUG (2021) p. 24, polar configuration: "Surface Operations Duration Up to 14 Days".

panelHeightM.note: Height of the solar panel above the ground used for the terrain horizon. Not published, and Griffin's height is not known either (only a 4.5 m width label); the model default of 2 m is kept. Robustness row: 1 m and 3 m.

landingAccuracyM.note: Radius of the landing ellipse the verdict is re-checked over. Griffin has not landed yet; assumed between the results CLPS landers have demonstrated (Blue Ghost 100 m, Nova-C IM-2 400 m).

heatLossW.note: Heat the warm box radiates at +20 °C to a cold sky. Assumed: the radiators are sized to reject the day load (700 W) and keep radiating at night (no louvers or heat switches; CLPS landers are designed for daylight). At the -20 °C set point that is 389 W, minus what the ground gives back (LRO Diviner).

heatCapacityKJPerK.note: Thermal mass of the warm box: 10% of the dry mass assumed coupled to it (batteries, avionics, nearby structure), at aluminium's 0.897 kJ/(kg·K) → 179.4 kJ/K. Dry mass: dry mass not published; ~2,000 kg assumed (class estimate). Sets how long the box coasts after sunset before the heaters switch on.

operatingTempC.note: Warm-box temperature while lit and when darkness begins: within the 10–25 °C range recommended for long Li-ion battery life (EnerSys ABSL space battery datasheet). Not published for this lander.

minTempC.note: Heater set point: the box (battery) is never let below it at night. Space Li-ion cells are characterised for discharge at -20 °C and below (EnerSys, Space Power Workshop 2022); charging needs 0 °C or more, which the Sun brings back. Not published for this lander.

groundViewFactor.note: Share of the warm box's radiating area that sees the ground (side walls half ground, half sky; top deck sky; bottom ground). The rest radiates to the ~3 K sky. Geometric estimate.

modelNote: Visualisation only. APPROXIMATE: the model's largest horizontal extent is scaled to 4.5 m. Astrobotic's Griffin page (https://www.astrobotic.com/lunar-delivery/landers/griffin-lander/) labels a drawing "4.5M" but its text gives no dimensions, so the width is not confirmed. modelNozzleOffsetM: engine plume origin above the feet, visual estimate from the model's shape.
